name: astrocyte_neuron_tripartite
description: Astrocyte senses synaptic activity and returns a slow modulatory signal.

name: axo_axonic
description: Axon terminal onto the axon initial segment; gates spike initiation without touching the soma.

name: axo_dendrite_reciprocal
description: Reciprocal pair: one direction excitatory, the return direction inhibitory (olfactory-bulb style).

name: axo_dendritic
description: Axon terminal onto dendritic shaft/spine; the default cortical excitatory contact.

name: axo_somatic
description: Axon terminal onto soma; perisomatic, strongly shunting (basket-cell style).

name: contrast_inhibition
description: Inhibition proportional to local stimulus energy; normalises the population response.

name: dendritic_computation
description: Non-linear dendritic integration (NMDA spikes, plateau potentials) as a local operator.

name: dendritic_excitatory_synapse
description: Excitatory contact placed on a specific dendritic branch; branch-local integration.

name: dendritic_inhibitory_synapse
description: Inhibitory contact on a dendritic branch; vetoes a branch without somatic shunting.

name: dendro_dendritic
description: Direct dendro-dendritic contact; allows subthreshold crosstalk and reciprocal pairs.

name: disinhibition
description: A -> interneuron -| target: exciting the interneuron releases the target.

name: ephaptic_coupling
description: Non-synaptic field coupling; activity in one fibre changes the excitability of a neighbour. Span is 'either', because a field does not respect a unit boundary -- an electric organ drives its own receptors across tissues.

name: feedback_excitatory
description: Higher stage re-excites an earlier stage; sustains and amplifies a representation.

name: feedback_inhibitory
description: Higher stage returns inhibition to an earlier stage; predictive suppression.

name: feedforward_excitatory
description: A -> B -> C all excitatory; signal relayed and sharpened across stages.

name: feedforward_gating
description: A gating population multiplicatively admits or blocks a throughput path.

name: feedforward_inhibitory
description: Input excites both a target and an interneuron that inhibits the target; narrows the time window.

name: gap_junction_inhibitory
description: Gap junction onto an inhibitory population; synchronises the local brake.

name: gap_junction_sync
description: Bidirectional electrotonic coupling; equalises membrane potential, zero delay.

name: global_inhibitory_gain_control
description: One wide-field inhibitory cell sums the whole population and feeds back onto all of it, enforcing sparseness (APL onto Kenyon cells).

name: inhibitory_hub
description: A single inhibitory hub broadcasts to a very large target set (MaleCNS-extracted).

name: lateral_feedback
description: Lateral partner both feeds forward and receives feedback; forms a resonant ring.

name: lateral_inhibitory
description: Neighbouring units inhibit each other; sharpens contrast and sparsifies the code.

name: ltp_ltd
description: Sustained activity produces durable bidirectional weight change.

name: modulatory_diffuse
description: One modulatory source broadcasts a scalar gain over many targets; no point-to-point map.

name: mutual_inhibitory
description: Two populations inhibit each other; produces winner-take-all or alternation.

name: neuromodulatory_axon
description: Axon with en-passant varicosities releasing along its length, not at one terminal.

name: pre_presynaptic_excitation
description: Excitation applied to a presynaptic terminal; boosts release probability.

name: pre_presynaptic_inhibition
description: Inhibition applied to a presynaptic terminal; attenuates release downstream.

name: recurrent_excitatory
description: Population excites itself through a loop; attractor / persistent activity.

name: recurrent_feedback
description: Closed loop between two stages with a delay; the MaleCNS-extracted third original motif.

name: recurrent_inhibitory
description: Loop where inhibition dominates; keeps activity bounded and rhythmic.

name: repetitive_activation_lts
description: A brief run of presynaptic spikes produces a lasting increase in release that outlives the train by many minutes -- the cephalopod vertical-lobe rule.

name: reservoir_smallworld
description: High-clustering, short-path recurrent pool used as a random-feature reservoir (MaleCNS-extracted).

name: retrograde_messenger
description: Postsynaptic cell releases a messenger that acts back on the presynaptic terminal.

name: serotonergic_presynaptic_facilitation
description: A modulatory terminal raises release probability in the sensory neuron without any postsynaptic depolarisation -- the mechanism of sensitisation in the Aplysia gill-withdrawal reflex, i.e. a memory stored presynaptically.

name: short_range_volume
description: Locally confined diffusion; a middle case between a synapse and full volume release.

name: short_term_habituation
description: Repeated activation of the same pathway depresses release, so the same stimulus produces a progressively smaller response and recovers in minutes -- the counterweight to presynaptic facilitation.

name: short_term_plasticity
description: Vesicle depletion / residual calcium give seconds-scale facilitation or depression.

name: shunting_inhibition
description: Inhibition lowers input resistance rather than hyperpolarising; divisive gain control.

name: stdp_rule
description: Pre-before-post potentiates, post-before-pre depresses; timing-based weight change.

name: temporal_coherence
description: Co-active populations phase-align; binding by synchrony rather than by weight.

name: thermal_cross_modal_convergence
description: An infrared map and a visual map registered onto the same tectal neurons, so a warm target is localised in the same coordinates as a seen one and either modality can drive the strike (pit vipers; vampire bats).

name: topographic_mapping
description: Spatially ordered projection preserving neighbourhood relations across stages.

name: volume_transmission
description: Transmitter diffuses through extracellular space and reaches non-synaptic receptors.
